chili_cercospora.cause: Fungal disease caused by Cercospora capsici, spreading rapidly in warm, humid climates with frequent rain.
symptoms: Circular brown spots with gray centers on leaves
Yellow haloid rings around infected leaf lesions
Premature leaf drying and defoliation
chili_cercospora.pesticides: Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5g/L water), Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (3g/L), or Chlorothalonil 75% WP.
chili_cercospora.organic_nutrients: Neem Oil spray (5ml/L + soap), Trichoderma viride bio-fungicide, Vermicompost & Neem Cake in root zone.
chili_cercospora.inorganic_nutrients: NPK 19-19-19 foliar spray (5g/L) for plant recovery, Calcium Nitrate to strengthen cell walls.
chili_cercospora.treatment: Spray recommended fungicide immediately. Remove and destroy infected fallen leaves.
chili_cercospora.prevention: Avoid overhead watering, maintain plant spacing for air flow, use certified disease-free seeds.

chili_powdery_mildew.cause: Fungal infection by Leveillula taurica thriving in dry weather with high relative humidity.
symptoms: White powdery coating on leaf lower surface
Yellowish patches on upper leaf surface
Upward curling and premature shedding of leaves
chili_powdery_mildew.pesticides: Wettable Sulphur 80% WP (3g/L), Hexaconazole 5% EC (1ml/L), or Dinocap.
chili_powdery_mildew.organic_nutrients: Potassium Bicarbonate spray (3g/L), Neem oil + baking soda solution, Sour buttermilk / whey spray (1:9 ratio).
chili_powdery_mildew.inorganic_nutrients: Micronutrient mixture spray (Zinc & Boron), Muriate of Potash (MOP) for leaf immunity.
chili_powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur or hexaconazole fungicide at early onset of white patches.
chili_powdery_mildew.prevention: Ensure good sunlight, avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizers, keep field weed-free.

chili_mites_and_trips.cause: Microscopic sap-sucking pests (Polyphagotarsonemus latus and Scirtothrips dorsalis).
symptoms: Downward leaf curling (Mites) or Upward leaf curling (Thrips)
Rough, silvery or bronze texture under leaves
Stunted growth and floral drop
chili_mites_and_trips.pesticides: Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (1ml/L for Mites), Fipronil 5% SC (1.5ml/L) or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL.
chili_mites_and_trips.organic_nutrients: Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%), Garlic-Chili extract spray, Blue & Yellow sticky traps.
chili_mites_and_trips.inorganic_nutrients: Zinc Sulphate (2g/L) + Ferrous Sulphate spray to overcome sap-loss chlorosis.
chili_mites_and_trips.treatment: Alternate miticide/insecticide sprays every 7-10 days to break pest lifecycle.
chili_mites_and_trips.prevention: Install yellow/blue sticky traps, spray neem oil regularly, maintain field hygiene.

chili_healthy.cause: No disease detected; chili plant displays robust health.
symptoms: Vibrant green leaves without discoloration
Healthy stems and active flowering/fruiting
Normal uncurled foliage
chili_healthy.organic_nutrients: Panchagavya spray (3%), Vermicompost (200g/plant), Cow dung manure, Mustard cake tea.
chili_healthy.inorganic_nutrients: Balanced NPK 19-19-19 (3g/L), Epsom salt (Magnesium Sulphate 2g/L) for lush greening.
chili_healthy.treatment: No treatment needed. Continue standard agricultural care.
chili_healthy.prevention: Maintain scheduled irrigation, balanced nutrition, and routine crop scouting.

mango_anthracnose.cause: Fungal pathogen Colletotrichum gloeosporioides spread by rain splashes and high humidity.
symptoms: Dark brown to black angular spots on leaves
Blossom blight and dark sunken lesions on fruits
Tear-staining pattern on developing mangoes
mango_anthracnose.pesticides: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (3g/L), Carbendazim 50% WP (1g/L), or Azoxystrobin 23% SC.
mango_anthracnose.organic_nutrients: Pseudomonas fluorescens (5g/L spray), Neem cake applied around tree basin, Bio-compost.
mango_anthracnose.inorganic_nutrients: Potassium Nitrate (NPK 13-0-45 10g/L) to boost fruit set, Boron (1.5g/L).
mango_anthracnose.treatment: Prune dead twigs before monsoon and spray Copper Oxychloride or Carbendazim.
mango_anthracnose.prevention: Destroy fallen leaves and fruits, maintain tree canopy ventilation through pruning.

mango_bacterial_canker.cause: Bacterial pathogen Xanthomonas citri pv. mangiferaeindicae.
symptoms: Water-soaked dark brown spots on leaves with yellow halos
Cankerous raised cracks on stems and twigs
Gummy exudation and dark star-shaped fruit cracks
mango_bacterial_canker.pesticides: Streptocycline (1g/10L water) mixed with Copper Oxychloride (2.5g/L).
mango_bacterial_canker.organic_nutrients: Cow dung slurry spray (filtered), Trichoderma harzianum soil application, Humic acid granules.
mango_bacterial_canker.inorganic_nutrients: Zinc Sulphate (2g/L) & Calcium Chloride (3g/L) spray to strengthen plant tissue.
mango_bacterial_canker.treatment: Spray Streptocycline + Copper fungicide twice at 15-day intervals.
mango_bacterial_canker.prevention: Avoid mechanical injury to trees, use disease-free nursery grafts, sanitize pruning tools.

mango_cutting_weevil.cause: Deporaus marginatus weevil cutting young reddish tender mango leaves.
symptoms: Freshly cut young leaves hanging or found on ground
Semicircular cuts on leaf margins
Loss of new vegetative flushes
mango_cutting_weevil.pesticides: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (2ml/L) or Quinalphos 25% EC (2ml/L) sprayed on new leaf flush.
mango_cutting_weevil.organic_nutrients: Beauveria bassiana bio-insecticide (5g/L), Neem oil 10,000 PPM (3ml/L), Wood ash at tree base.
mango_cutting_weevil.inorganic_nutrients: Complex NPK 10-26-26 (500g/tree), Single Super Phosphate (SSP) for root vigor.
mango_cutting_weevil.treatment: Spray recommended insecticide as soon as new reddish leaf flushes emerge.
mango_cutting_weevil.prevention: Collect and burn fallen cut leaves containing weevil eggs, rake soil under canopy.

mango_die_back.cause: Fungal disease caused by Lasiodiplodia theobromae infecting pruned or injured branches.
symptoms: Drying of twigs and branches starting from top downwards
Leaves turn brown, roll, and remain attached to dead twigs
Internal browning of stem tissue
mango_die_back.pesticides: Prune affected twigs 2-3 inches below dead area and apply Bordeaux paste (10%) or Copper Oxychloride paste.
mango_die_back.organic_nutrients: Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer in soil, Well-rotted Farmyard Manure (FYM 50kg/tree).
mango_die_back.inorganic_nutrients: Sulphate of Potash (SOP 500g/tree), Micronutrient mix containing Zinc, Manganese & Iron.
mango_die_back.treatment: Cut infected branches cleanly and immediately coat cut ends with copper paste.
mango_die_back.prevention: Avoid branch injury during harvesting, paint trunk with lime-copper paste before monsoon.

mango_gall_midge.cause: Procontarinia spp. midge flies laying eggs inside young leaf tissues.
symptoms: Wart-like small galls or pimple swells on leaves
Leaf distortion, shot-holes, and premature leaf fall
Reduced tree photosynthesis
mango_gall_midge.pesticides: Dimethoate 30% EC (1.5ml/L) or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (0.5ml/L) at flush stage.
mango_gall_midge.organic_nutrients: Metarhizium anisopliae bio-pesticide, Neem cake application in basin (2kg/tree).
mango_gall_midge.inorganic_nutrients: Urea (nitrogen for new leaf regrowth), Magnesium Sulphate for chlorophyll synthesis.
mango_gall_midge.treatment: Spray systemic insecticide when new leaf buds begin unfolding.
mango_gall_midge.prevention: Deep plow tree basins in summer to destroy pupae in soil, prune heavily infested branches.

mango_healthy.cause: No infection found; mango leaves are vigorous and disease-free.
symptoms: Deep green, glossy leathery foliage
Strong terminal buds and healthy canopy structure
No spots, galls, or powdery patches
mango_healthy.organic_nutrients: Well-rotted FYM (50kg/tree), Neem Cake (3kg/tree), Bio-fertilizers (Azospirillum & PSB).
mango_healthy.inorganic_nutrients: NPK 10-26-26 (1-2 kg/tree based on age), Micronutrient foliar spray before flowering.
mango_healthy.prevention: Follow annual fertilization cycle post-harvest, maintain orchard sanitation.

mango_powdery_mildew.cause: Oidium mangiferae fungal parasite damaging inflorescences and leaves during cool dry nights.
symptoms: White powdery coating on flowers, panicles, and tender leaves
Browning and dropping of flowers (Blossom drop)
Deformed, crinkled young leaves
mango_powdery_mildew.pesticides: Wettable Sulphur 80% WP (3g/L), Hexaconazole 5% EC (1ml/L), or Myclobutanil 10% WP.
mango_powdery_mildew.organic_nutrients: Potassium Bicarbonate (3g/L) + Neem Oil, Sour cow milk whey solution.
mango_powdery_mildew.inorganic_nutrients: Potassium Nitrate (13-0-45 5g/L) for fruit retention, Soluble Boron.
mango_powdery_mildew.treatment: Spray Wettable Sulphur or Hexaconazole at panicle emergence and fruit set stage.
mango_powdery_mildew.prevention: Prune dense inner branches to permit sunlight penetration into canopy.

mango_sooty_mould.cause: Capnodium mangiferae fungus growing on honeydew excreted by aphids, scales, or mealybugs.
symptoms: Black velvety charcoal-like layer covering leaves and twigs
Stunted growth due to blocked sunlight and reduced photosynthesis
Flakes of black crust peeling off dried leaves
mango_sooty_mould.pesticides: Spray Starch solution (1kg wheat flour boiled in 5L water, diluted to 20L water) to peel off mould. Spray Imidacloprid (0.5ml/L) to kill honeydew insects.
mango_sooty_mould.organic_nutrients: Neem oil (5ml/L) + Soft potassic soap spray, Vermicompost in basin.
mango_sooty_mould.inorganic_nutrients: NPK 19-19-19 (4g/L) foliar spray after cleaning black mould layer.
mango_sooty_mould.treatment: First kill sap-sucking insects with insecticide/neem oil, then apply starch spray to flake off black layer.
mango_sooty_mould.prevention: Control hoppers, aphids, and scale insects early in the season.

potato_bacteria.cause: Ralstonia solanacearum or Pectobacterium species infecting vascular system.
symptoms: Rapid wilting of leaves during warm day hours
Stems show dark brown vascular ring discoloration
Soft, foul-smelling rot inside potato tubers
potato_bacteria.pesticides: Copper Hydroxide 77% WP (2g/L) or Streptocycline (1g/10L) for seed tuber treatment.
potato_bacteria.organic_nutrients: Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/kg seed treatment), Mustard oil cake, Vermicompost.
potato_bacteria.inorganic_nutrients: Calcium Nitrate (5g/L) to reinforce plant cell walls against bacterial enzymes, Potassium Sulphate.
potato_bacteria.treatment: Rogue out and destroy infected plants immediately. Drench surrounding soil with copper solution.
potato_bacteria.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers, practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.

potato_fungi.cause: Alternaria solani or Fusarium species causing foliar leaf spot and wilt.
symptoms: Target-board concentric brown rings on older leaves
Yellowing surrounding dark brown circular spots
Dry rot and leaf shriveling
potato_fungi.pesticides: Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5g/L), Chlorothalonil 75% WP (2g/L), or Difenoconazole 25% EC.
potato_fungi.organic_nutrients: Trichoderma viride bio-fungicide (5g/L), Neem oil 10,000 PPM, Bio-fertilizers (VAM / Mycorrhiza).
potato_fungi.inorganic_nutrients: NPK 12-61-0 (Mono Ammonium Phosphate 4g/L) for leaf recovery, Zinc Sulphate (2g/L).
potato_fungi.treatment: Apply Mancozeb or Difenoconazole spray at first sight of target-ring spots.
potato_fungi.prevention: Avoid nitrogen deficiency, maintain proper plant spacing, eliminate solanaceous weeds.

potato_healthy.cause: No pathogen detected; potato foliage is thriving with healthy green vigor.
symptoms: Uniform deep green leaf canopy without spots or curling
Sturdy upright stems
Healthy root and stolon development
potato_healthy.organic_nutrients: Well-decomposed compost (10 tons/acre), Vermicompost, Neem cake, Bone meal.
potato_healthy.inorganic_nutrients: NPK 10-26-26 (at earthing up), Magnesium Sulphate (Epsom salt 3g/L) for tuber starch boost.
potato_healthy.prevention: Maintain regular hilling/earthing up, balanced soil moisture, and pest monitoring.

potato_nematode.cause: Microscopic soil nematodes (Meloidogyne spp. or Globodera spp.) attacking roots.
symptoms: Stunted growth, patchiness in potato field
Yellowing leaves resembling nutrient deficiency
Small galls or tiny cyst swellings on roots and small tubers
potato_nematode.pesticides: Fluopyram 400 SC (Velum Prime 1ml/2L) or Cartap Hydrochloride 4% Granules in soil.
potato_nematode.organic_nutrients: Neem cake application (250 kg/acre), Purpureocillium lilacinum bio-agent, Marigold green manure.
potato_nematode.inorganic_nutrients: High Potash NPK 0-0-50 (Sulfate of Potash 5g/L) for tuber weight & stress tolerance.
potato_nematode.treatment: Apply bio-nematicide or Fluopyram drench around plant base.
potato_nematode.prevention: Rotate crops with Marigold (Tagetes), apply Neem cake generously during soil preparation.

potato_pest.cause: Insects feeding on potato foliage and transmitting viral pathogens.
symptoms: Visible holes, chewed leaf margins, or skeletonized foliage
Clusters of green/black aphids under leaves
Curled sticky leaves covered with honeydew
potato_pest.pesticides: Thiamethoxam 25% WG (0.5g/L), Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (0.4ml/L), or Acephate 75% SP.
potato_pest.organic_nutrients: Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%), Beauveria bassiana (5g/L), Yellow sticky cards.
potato_pest.inorganic_nutrients: NPK 19-19-19 (3g/L) + Micronutrient mix (Iron, Zinc, Manganese) for tissue repair.
potato_pest.treatment: Spray Thiamethoxam or Acephate to control sap-sucking aphids and leaf beetles.
potato_pest.prevention: Install yellow sticky traps (20/acre), monitor crop weekly, eliminate field weeds.

potato_phytophthora.cause: Destructive oomycete pathogen Phytophthora infestans favoured by cool, foggy, wet weather.
symptoms: Water-soaked dark brown to black lesions on leaf tips and margins
White cottony fungal downy growth on underside of leaves in humid mornings
Rapid foliage destruction and brown rotting tubers
potato_phytophthora.pesticides: Systemic fungicide: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil Gold 2.5g/L), Dimethomorph 50% WP (1g/L), or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb.
potato_phytophthora.organic_nutrients: Bordeaux Mixture (1% spray), Trichoderma harzianum soil treatment, Organic Seaweed Extract.
potato_phytophthora.inorganic_nutrients: Calcium Nitrate + Boron (5g/L) to strengthen plant cell walls against zoospores.
potato_phytophthora.treatment: Spray Ridomil Gold or Dimethomorph immediately upon first symptom; repeat in 7 days if wet weather continues.
potato_phytophthora.prevention: Destroy volunteer potato plants, avoid flood irrigation, plant resistant cultivars.

potato_virus.cause: Viral pathogens transmitted by aphid vector insects and infected seed tubers.
symptoms: Mosaic light and dark green leaf mottle patterns
Leaf crinkling, puckering, and downward rolling
Stunted vine growth and severe tuber yield reduction
potato_virus.pesticides: No chemical cure exists for viral infection. Spray Systemic Insecticide (Acetamiprid 20% SP 0.5g/L or Imidacloprid) to eliminate aphid vector insects.
potato_virus.organic_nutrients: Neem Oil 10,000 PPM (3ml/L) to deter aphids, Humic Acid + Seaweed Extract for vine vigor.
potato_virus.inorganic_nutrients: Sulphate of Potash (SOP 0-0-50 5g/L) + Zinc Sulphate to support surviving green foliage.
potato_virus.treatment: Rogue out (dig up and burn) infected virus plants to prevent spread to surrounding healthy crop.
potato_virus.prevention: Always use certified virus-free seed tubers, control aphid populations early with sticky traps.
